meaningOfAccept: An accepted row means a cited source supports that the polity existed on 25 December 800 and held roughly the polygon, and mapMappings approves the polygon as approximate gameplay geometry. It approves no vertex, frontier or uniform control. Each noteSv states the limit. Unverified names and extents remain unresolved. Cultural labels do not establish sovereign rulers or researched occupancy.
default: Unnamed features and unreviewed land stay unresolved and render as Okänd historisk kontroll.

calendar.handling: The date is a game label in the proleptic Gregorian game calendar with no year zero. Sources keep their own chronology and this file converts no day. The Royal Frankish Annals count the year from Christmas and enter the coronation under 801.

rfa-800-itinerary.locator: Annales regni Francorum, ed. Kurze, MGH SS rer. Germ. 6 (1895), pp. 110-111, s.a. 800
rfa-800-itinerary.scopedClaim: Charles left Aachen in mid-March, went by the coast and Rouen to Tours, and stayed there because his wife Liutgard was ill. She died and was buried there. He returned to Aachen by Orleans and Paris. In the original text (p. 110) he reached Mainz in early August and announced the Italian journey. The revised text (p. 111) adds a general assembly at Mainz.
rfa-800-itinerary.calendarHandling: Latin church-calendar date as printed by Kurze; no conversion to the game calendar

rfa-800-italy.locator: Annales regni Francorum, ed. Kurze, MGH SS rer. Germ. 6 (1895), pp. 110-111, s.a. 800
rfa-800-italy.scopedClaim: Charles took an army to Ravenna, ordered an expedition against the Beneventans and sent his son Pippin with the army to raid their land. The revised text adds that father and son moved to Ancona, where Charles left Pippin before going on to Rome.
rfa-800-italy.sourceDateWording: Between early August and 23 November 800; the annals state no season and no day for the parting at Ancona
rfa-800-italy.calendarHandling: Latin church-calendar date as printed by Kurze; no conversion to the game calendar

rfa-800-rome.locator: Annales regni Francorum, ed. Kurze, MGH SS rer. Germ. 6 (1895), pp. 110-112, s.a. 800
rfa-800-rome.scopedClaim: Leo met Charles at Nomentum on 23 November and received him at St Peter's the next day. After seven days an assembly heard charges against the pope, no accuser came forward to prove them, and Leo cleared himself by oath. Charles kept Christmas in Rome.
rfa-800-rome.sourceDateWording: Kurze margin Nov. 23, Nov. 24, Dec. 23; the Dec. 23 margin date comes from the Lorsch chronicle, n. 1, and the annal text states no date for the oath
rfa-800-rome.calendarHandling: Latin church-calendar date as printed by Kurze; no conversion to the game calendar

rfa-801-coronation.locator: Annales regni Francorum, ed. Kurze, MGH SS rer. Germ. 6 (1895), p. 112, s.a. 801
rfa-801-coronation.scopedClaim: On Christmas Day at mass before the confession of St Peter, Leo placed a crown on Charles and the Roman people acclaimed him. The title patricius gave way to imperator et augustus. The annalist has already changed the year number to 801 at this point.
rfa-801-coronation.sourceDateWording: in ipso sacratissimo die natalis Domini; year changed to 801
rfa-801-coronation.calendarHandling: The annalist counts the year from Christmas, so the entry year can differ from a January count; no conversion

rfa-801-aftermath.locator: Annales regni Francorum, ed. Kurze, MGH SS rer. Germ. 6 (1895), pp. 112-114, s.a. 801
rfa-801-aftermath.scopedClaim: The conspirators Paschalis and Campulus were condemned under Roman law after the coronation, the pope interceded, and they went into exile. Charles spent the winter ordering Rome and Italy, sent Pippin against the Beneventans again, and left Rome on 25 April for Spoleto.
rfa-801-aftermath.calendarHandling: Latin church-calendar date as printed by Kurze; no conversion to the game calendar

rfa-801-barcelona.locator: Annales regni Francorum, ed. Kurze, MGH SS rer. Germ. 6 (1895), p. 116, s.a. 801
rfa-801-barcelona.scopedClaim: Barcelona fell that summer after a two-year siege and its prefect Zatun was captured. In Italy Chieti was taken and burned, its prefect Roselmus was captured, and the castles belonging to the city surrendered.
rfa-801-barcelona.calendarHandling: Latin church-calendar date as printed by Kurze; no conversion to the game calendar

rfa-797-barcelona.locator: Annales regni Francorum, ed. Kurze, MGH SS rer. Germ. 6 (1895), pp. 100-101, s.a. 797
